table4_sensitivity: CG-RJMCMC one-factor sensitivity results. RMSE entries are median [IQR] across 100 independent replications per modified setting on the log-RT scale. Correct $K$ denotes recovery by the empirical joint MAP partition; $n$ gives the completed replication count. The maximum-count setting below the true count excludes the generating partition by construction.
table1_design: Simulation design and reproducibility settings. $N$ is the number of participants, $T=64$ is the number of progression bins, and true levels are congruency effects on the log-RT scale. Common CG-RJMCMC settings are fixed at $K_{\max}=4$, minimum segment length 8 bins, 3 chains, 15000 iterations per chain, and 2000 warm-up iterations.
table2_rmse: Trajectory estimation and held-out prediction error. Entries are medians across 500 independently generated datasets per DGP--method cell. Trajectory RMSE is on the congruency-effect log-RT scale; held-out test RMSE is on the individual log-RT scale. PELT-BIC uses minimum-length-safe unrestricted PELT with the prespecified penalty.
table3_structural_recovery: Structural recovery by change-point method across 500 independently generated datasets per DGP--method cell. Hausdorff distance is in progression bins (defined as 64 when one partition has no boundary and the other does); Hausdorff and segment-level RMSE are median [IQR]. Level RMSE is conditional on recovering the correct number of segments; $n_K$ is its denominator. Correct $K$ is the proportion of replications in which the selected complete partition has the true number of changes; CG-RJMCMC uses the joint MAP partition. PELT-BIC uses the corrected unrestricted PELT solver.
table4_computation_sensitivity: CG-RJMCMC diagnostics across 500 independently generated datasets per DGP. Pass rate applies the prespecified screening rule to the monitored count and two trajectory coordinates; a count constant across all chains has no defined diagnostic. Entries are median [IQR] across applicable replications. ESS denotes bulk ESS. Runtime is three-chain execution time in seconds, excluding preprocessing, posterior aggregation, diagnostics, and file operations.
